clue.text: Independent member's back in political party? Very good

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the party's initials

parts.note: the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

indicators.note: going back means the pair before it is read from right to left

parts.note: standard abbreviation for an independent candidate
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an independent MP's return to a party is a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' applies to both the abbreviation and the limb together, so the pair is turned round as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A child described as angelic behaves beautifully, so the adjective serves as praise for excellent conduct.

clue.text: Old man, emasculated and quite sad

indicators.note: emasculated means losing the male, so the letter M for male is removed
sad in its sense of sorry or wretched suggests the letters are in a poor, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A sorry description of an elderly man who has lost his virility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like a single phrase, but Old is the definition and man is wordplay; M is the abbreviation for male.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an object from long ago, and the word also works as an adjective for anything aged.

clue.text: One whose number is up, having rounded Lido recklessly?

definitions.text: One whose number is up, having rounded Lido recklessly?

indicators.note: rounding something means going all the way about it, so the doomed one surrounds the other letters
reckless movement throws the letters of the resort name into disorder

explanation.surface: A boatman tearing round the Venice Lido so wildly he may not survive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and picture: the Lido is the Venetian beach island, where a gondolier works.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman steering a gondola round the Lido at speed would plausibly be risking his life.

clue.text: Early craft houses (synthetic material)

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, holding it within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters span the join between the two words

explanation.surface: An early boat sheltering something made of man-made fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a trade name for a stretchy elastane fibre manufactured chemically rather than grown naturally.

clue.text: Insect represented on chalice

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bug pictured in the decoration of a church cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochineal is a scale bug of Mexico, crushed to make a crimson dye that shares its name.

clue.text: Stage play after Oedipus Rex leads switched

indicators.note: after places the word for play behind the swapped letters
switched means the two front letters swap places
leads are the front letters of the two words of the title

parts.note: first letters of the play's title
to strum is to play a guitar casually

explanation.surface: Putting on a production of Sophocles' tragedy with its lead actors swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage play' reads as one phrase, but Stage is the definition and play the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor, a small stage to stand on.

clue.text: Mature stripe not at the centre

indicators.note: only the middle part of the phrase is kept, with the outer letters dropped from each end

parts.note: the central five letters, losing two from each end

explanation.surface: A grown-up stripe that is placed somewhere other than the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to grow fully developed, the verb sense of mature as fruit or cheese ages.

clue.text: Wrongly take fruit (the Niçoise date) that's crushed

parts.note: to scrump is to steal apples from an orchard, a British word
the French for 'the', as said in Nice

explanation.surface: Stolen fruit, a date from Nice included, ends up squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Niçoise means from Nice, so 'the' is put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpled is a dialect form meaning crumpled or squashed out of shape, like paper screwed up.

clue.text: OK bloke's name?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: radio operators' word for message received and understood
second meaning: a common male first name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like asking whether a man's name is acceptable; the radio sense of acknowledgement is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio talk the word confirms a message is received, much like okay, and it is also a man's forename.

clue.text: Artist lives by sealing lead in china

indicators.note: in puts the joined pieces inside the word for china

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to live is to be, so lives is

indicators.note: a lead is the front, so only the opening letter of sealing is kept

explanation.surface: A painter living near a factory sealing lead inside porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not porcelain but Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famous for bold colour and late paper cut-outs.

clue.text: Stimulant that's popular in bed, perversely

indicators.note: perversely means the wrong way round, so the combination is read backwards
in places the word for popular inside the word for bed

explanation.surface: A saucy hint at something that perks things up between the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is anything that invigorates or restores energy, such as a medicine or pick-me-up.

clue.text: Reproductive control of ape, correct?

explanation.surface: A query about birth control for a gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproductive' suggests breeding, but here it means making reproductions of a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal power over who may reproduce a creative work, hence control of reproduction.

clue.text: They confine 'sub-atomic particles keeping motion at variance'

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the particles hold the rearranged letters within them

parts.note: quarks are the elementary particles inside protons and neutrons

indicators.note: at variance means in disagreement or disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A physics statement about particles, conveniently set in inverted commas.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is illustrated by the clue itself, whose wordplay sits between the very marks being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas enclose quoted speech or text, so they hem in or confine the words between them.

clue.text: See 11
One's doing U-turn — court put out

indicators.note: a U-turn sends things back the way they came, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: one has, or I have, contracted

explanation.surface: Someone turning round as a court throws them out.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as 'one has', which becomes the first-person I've.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from a property, putting them out of their home.

clue.text: Extremely tentative about a simple, radical sort of photography

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the end letters go around the rearranged ones
extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of tentative
a radical change is a thorough upheaval, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A cautious take on a straightforward yet revolutionary photographic technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at intervals so slow change, like a flower opening, plays back quickly.

clue.text: English version of 'Up Attlee' uniform decoration

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so the quoted letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English rendering of a slogan backing Clement Attlee, the post-war Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the ornamental shoulder piece sewn on a military or naval uniform coat.

clue.text: A riotous assembly swamps college — ghastly

indicators.note: swamps means engulfs, so the rebuilt letters surround the abbreviation
an assembly puts parts together anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd of protesters overwhelming a college, a dreadful scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious and ghastly both describe something horrifyingly bad or of appallingly poor quality.

clue.text: Maybe Pepys' daughter going after head gardener

indicators.note: daughter going means the abbreviation D departs from the word
after places what is left behind the word for head

parts.note: the top is the head of something
Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London; maybe marks him as an example

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Samuel Pepys's daughter went off chasing the head gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepys' is not possessive here: it stands for a diarist, the role he is famous for.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist is a garden worker who clips hedges and shrubs into ornamental shapes.

clue.text: It makes no sense of call from South Carolina windbag

definitions.text: It makes no sense of call

parts.note: someone who talks at length aimlessly

explanation.surface: A long-winded talker from South Carolina whose phone calls make no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is a device that garbles a telephone signal so eavesdroppers cannot understand the conversation.

clue.text: Shooter's recommended action for ducks and drakes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pistol worn at the hip, read as shooter is

definitions.text: recommended action for ducks and drakes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the low, flat throwing style used for skimming stones

explanation.walkthrough: Ducks and drakes is the game of skipping flat stones across water, not birds; a shooter is a gun, and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A holstered handgun is called this, and the same word names a low throw with the arm held level, ideal for skipping stones.

clue.text: Remove a plant from its container and store?

definitions.text: Remove a plant from its container
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., to take out of a pot
second meaning: a warehouse or storage place

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an invented verb: de- plus pot, as in unpotting a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse where goods or vehicles are kept, and split as de-pot it means unpot.

clue.text: As a consequence of your once imbibing free beer

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the old word for your takes in the loosened letters
free means let loose, so the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: The result of having downed some beer you got for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means or as a result of that, linking an outcome to its cause.

clue.text: Valentine card I designed for utterly evil type

indicators.note: designed means drawn up afresh, so the letters are laid out to a new plan

explanation.surface: Someone made a Valentine card for a thoroughly wicked person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person so wicked they seem to be Satan himself in human form.

clue.text: Former queen hugging toe-curling cross-maker?

indicators.note: hugging means holding close, so the old royal initials wrap round the other letters

parts.note: Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria's royal cipher

indicators.note: curling bends something out of its straight line, so its letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria embracing an angry person whose toes curl in annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks a cross beside the chosen candidate on a ballot paper, so makes a cross.

clue.text: See 21
Unfit, one needs 'sleep time'

explanation.surface: Someone out of condition needs a period of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate for the purpose, not fit for the job.

clue.text: Steps inside Forum ballroom

indicators.note: inside means the answer lies within the run of letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Dancing in a ballroom called the Forum.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, a set pattern of steps, so the plural noun stands for it.

clue.text: A line on summit, one hidden by — look! — a plateau

indicators.note: hidden by means covered by, so one sits inside the exclamation

parts.note: old word meaning look or behold
an means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Standing on a mountain top and pointing out a high flat expanse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Altiplano is the high Andean plain of Bolivia and Peru; on means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word means high plain, and it names the vast elevated tableland in the central Andes.

clue.text: Grass one put in labyrinth

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the numeral goes within the word for labyrinth

explanation.surface: Planting turf in a garden maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is a cereal crop belonging botanically to the grass family, like wheat.

clue.text: Musical ornamentation giving increasingly hollow sound

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to go by how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: increasingly means more, and a hollow is a dent

explanation.surface: A musical flourish that makes an ever emptier noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mordent is a quick ornament in music: a rapid alternation of the written note with the one below or above.

clue.text: Dark-hued cast put round growth

indicators.note: put round means placed around, so the throw surrounds the growth

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A tanned acting company gathered round a tumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion, skin naturally deep in colour or weathered by sun.
